cover.intro: Event Tickets lets space operators sell tickets for events held in their space. Members book and pay through the Members Portal, and operators track sales from the Admin Panel.
objectives: Create a ticketed event in the Admin Panel
Configure pricing and capacity for each ticket type
cover.disclaimer: The content and images in this course are accurate as of publication but may change over time. Images are for illustration only and may differ from what appears on your system.

blocks.html: Previously, operators could list an event but had no way to charge for entry or limit attendance. Event Tickets adds ticket types, pricing, and capacity controls directly to the event form.

Each event can have one or more ticket types — for example Standard, VIP, or Early-bird. Each type has its own price and capacity, so you can run limited-release tiers without juggling separate events.

items.title: Pricing
items.html: Prices are set per ticket type at creation. You can update a price any time before the event starts; members who already purchased keep the price they paid.

items.title: Capacity rules
items.html: Capacity is enforced per ticket type. When a type sells out it stops appearing in the member booking flow automatically.

blocks.html: Ticket sales are final once the event starts. Refunds must be processed manually by the operator.

blocks.intro: Follow these steps to create a ticketed event.
steps: Click **Create event** and complete the event details.
Add at least one ticket type with a price and capacity.
blocks.summary: Your event now appears in the member booking flow with live availability.

questions.prompt: Where do operators create a ticketed event?
questions.correctFeedback: Correct — events live under Events > All events.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Not quite — check the Events area of the Admin Panel.

questions.prompt: Capacity limits apply per ticket type.
questions.correctFeedback: Correct — each ticket type has its own capacity.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Review the capacity rules: limits are per ticket type.

questions.prompt: The toggle that enables ticket sales on the event form is called ______.
questions.incorrectFeedback: It's the Sell tickets toggle on the event form.
